title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
technique: feature-level (second-to-top layer) autoregressive draft head with shifted token sequence to resolve feature uncertainty; tree drafts; lossless speculative sampling

optimized_metrics.evidence: Like other speculative sampling-based methods, EAGLE primarily focuses on latency rather than throughput.
The key to enhancing acceleration in speculative sampling lies in reducing the time overhead and improving the acceptance rate of the draft by the original LLM
doubled throughput, while maintaining the distribution of the generated text

headline_claim.text: For LLaMA2-Chat 70B, EAGLE achieved a latency speedup ratio of 2.7x-3.5x, doubled throughput, while maintaining the distribution of the generated text.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 1-2, Table 1 walltime speedup; Table 3 tokens/s

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Walltime speedup ratio: The actual test speedup ratio relative to vanilla autoregressive decoding.
metric_definitions.notes: single-stream at bs=1 in main results

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Average acceptance length τ: The average number of tokens accepted per forward pass of the target LLM.
We calculated the throughput for different bs and selected the maximum value. Both vanilla autoregressive decoding and EAGLE achieve maximum throughput at their respective maximum bs.
metric_definitions.notes: throughput ratio vs vanilla, each at its memory-limited max batch size (7 vs 8 on RTX 3090 for Vicuna 7B; 4 vs 5 for 70B on 4xA100); units not stated

load_regime: batch=1 for main results ("experiments with a batch size of 1"); small fixed batch sizes 1-4 and max-memory batch in §4.4; no request-rate load
tradeoff_acknowledged: Speedup diminishes as batch size grows (Vicuna 7B 2.90x at bs1 -> 2.76x at bs4; 70B 3.01x -> 2.40x); EAGLE needs slightly more CUDA memory so max batch is 7 vs 8.
extractor_notes: Abstract 'doubled throughput' is the Table 7 ratio at max batch size, a secondary result; method objective is single-sequence latency. Speedup ratios in figures copied from Medusa/Lookahead reports for comparison.
